blocks.text: *How your abilities work, and where they come from.*

In Unwritten, **your equipped weapon carries its own kit of active skills.** Equip a sword and your hotbar fills with that sword's abilities; swap to a bow and the bar becomes the bow's kit. There are no classes in Unwritten — your weapon is what defines your abilities, and changing weapons is how you change your loadout. A weapon's kit isn't arbitrary: it is what its **Unwritten** — the person the weapon is the last trace of — could do. See *The World of Unwritten*.
Every weapon rolls its own kit

Each weapon *type* has its own **pool of skills** — **3 ultimates** plus a set of normal skills (how many depends on the weapon; the pool is only as large as the weapon's identity naturally supports). You do not find them: every skill names the **mastery level** in its weapon at which you learn it, and some name a skill you must know first. Practise a sword and its pool opens to you, one skill at a time, in the order the weapon teaches them.

**Your ultimate points at your build.** Each weapon's three ultimates each steer toward a different playstyle — and which Ring stats to invest in — so the ultimate you roll is a hint at how to build that weapon.

So two of the same weapon can play very differently, and chasing the weapon (and the ultimate) *you* want is part of the hunt. That isn't randomness for its own sake: a dropped weapon remembers its wielder in fragments, and the skills it carries are **which memories surfaced this time**. Every skill in a weapon's pool reinforces that weapon's identity — so whatever you roll, it still plays like that weapon.
Skills don't level — your Ring powers them

A skill's raw strength doesn't come from ranking the skill up. Instead, **your Ring stats scale it** (see *Stats & the Ring*). The same skill is stronger in the hands of someone who invested the right stats. This is what keeps roles honest: a heal only pays off if you invested MP; a damage skill only hits hard if you invested Attack or Magic Attack.
What a skill is made of

items: **Its numbers** — how much damage, how many hits, how long it lasts, its mana cost, cooldown, cast time, range, and area.
**Its effects** — what it actually *does*.

blocks.text: Most skills are **active**: they take a hotbar slot, and you press them. They cost mana and use the cooldown, cast time, range, and area above.
Some are **passive**. A passive takes **no hotbar slot and is never pressed** — it waits for a specific moment in the fight and fires on its own. The moment it waits for is part of the skill:

items: **After you finish casting a particular skill** — uninterrupted. This is how one skill rides another: Lock Blades off Lunge, Unwavering off Guard Stance.
**When a basic attack of yours lands.** Momentum and Flow ride this one.
**When you begin a basic attack.**
**When a hit of yours deals damage.**
**When you kill something.** Encore rides this one.
**When you drop to low health.**
**When you take damage.**
**When you successfully parry.** Opening rides this one.

blocks.text: A passive **fires as a full skill** — the same visuals and the same effects an active would play. Only the trigger is different. It aims itself, too: a skill that needs a target lands on whatever set it off, and a skill that targets you always lands on you.
Skills are built from a catalog of effects. The common ones:

items: **Damage** — direct harm. A multi-hit strike splits one total across its hits.
**Heal** — restore health now.
**Shield** — raise an absorbing barrier that soaks a set amount of damage, then lapses.

**Raise a stat / lower a stat** — the workhorse. One effect moves one number on the sheet for a while: your damage, attack speed, cast speed, move speed, health or mana regeneration, accuracy, evasion, attack, defense, crit, max health or mana, life steal, mana leech, reflect, or how much damage you take. Everything that used to be a separate Haste, Guard, Regen or Buff is this one effect now.
**Status ailments** — Burn, Poison, and Bleed (damage over time), plus Stun, Freeze, and Silence.
**Parry charges** — each charge erases one incoming hit outright, then is spent.
**Brace charges** — each charge holds back one incoming hit and banks the damage instead; the whole debt lands when the window ends.
**Damage charges** — charges that make your next attacks land harder (or an enemy's land softer). One charge, one attack, spent whether it hits or misses.
**Immunity to being stopped** — a window where nothing flinches, stuns, freezes, silences, shoves or interrupts you.
**Taunt** — force monsters to attack you.
**Knockback / Pull** — shove enemies away or drag them in.
**Cleanse** — strip debuffs off yourself.
**Execute** — bonus damage that grows huge against low-health enemies.
**Dash / Teleport** — close distance in a rush, or blink to a target spot.
**Feed another skill** — add stacks to another skill's pile, or give that pile more time. This is how Encore keeps Blade Dance going, and how Flow feeds Momentum.

blocks.text: **Ultimate skills** are a special tier — the biggest thing a weapon does, at **40 mana** and a long cooldown rather than a charge meter. Every weapon's pool holds **3** of them, and each opens deep into that weapon's mastery: the sword's arrive at **30**, **45** and **60**.

text: *Status: the skill framework above is in place. Exact numbers, cooldowns, and each weapon's skill pool are still being tuned and drafted.*
